title: Henselian approximation of a given clopen affine group homomorphism
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative henselian local G-ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-g-ring], let $k=A/\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-residue-field], and let $\widehat A=\varprojlim_{r\geq1}A/\mathfrak m^r$ with its canonical $A$-algebra structure [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}P$ and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}Q$ be affine $A$-group schemes, where $P,Q$ are finitely presented commutative $A$-algebras [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Group structures consist of multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams, and homomorphisms preserve these operations. Write $X_R=X\times_A\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $Y_R=Y\times_A\operatorname{Spec}R$ for an $A$-algebra $R$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. If a given $\widehat A$-group homomorphism $v:X_{\widehat A}\to Y_{\widehat A}$ is both an open immersion and a closed immersion [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion], then there exists an $A$-group homomorphism $w:X\to Y$, also both an open and a closed immersion, whose scalar extension to $k$ equals $v_k$ under the canonical residue identification $\widehat A/\mathfrak m\widehat A=k$. Flatness, smoothness, commutativity of the group laws and diagonalizability are not assumed. No equality $w_{\widehat A}=v$ is asserted.

source.place: Agent finite-polynomial-certificate consequence of Tag 0AH5 (lemma-henselian-pair), with the maximal ideal and approximation order one: encode a Hopf map and a clopen factor isomorphism by finitely many polynomial equations and relation-membership witnesses. The encoding argument is recorded in report.md; this unsplit node contains only its statement.

proof.text: Choose finite presentations $P=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_a)$ and $Q=A[y_1,\ldots,y_m]/(s_1,\ldots,s_b)$. For any $A$-algebra $R$, put $P_R=R\otimes_AP$ and $Q_R=R\otimes_AQ$. The affine fibre-product theorem identifies their spectra with $X_R,Y_R$. The universal property of tensor product and polynomial evaluation identifies $P_R$ with $R[x]/(r)$: maps from either algebra to an $R$-algebra are precisely tuples satisfying the $r_i$; the mutually inverse maps send each variable to its namesake. Likewise $Q_R=R[y]/(s)$ and $P_R\otimes_RP_R=R[x,x']/(r(x),r(x'))$. These presentations hold for every $R$; no flatness is used.

source.place: Tags 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), 01JQ; elementary universal-property calculation from Tag 00F3 presentations

proof.text: Write $f^{\wedge}:Q_{\widehat A}\to P_{\widehat A}$ for the algebra map of $v$. Its image $U\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}Q_{\widehat A}$ is clopen, and $v$ identifies its source with the open subscheme $U$. Choose the idempotent $e^{\wedge}$ with $U=D(e^{\wedge})$. The affine-basic-open theorem identifies restriction to $U$ with localization at $e^{\wedge}$. For any idempotent $e$ in a ring $B$, the map $B\to B_e$ is surjective and has kernel $(1-e)B$: in $B_e$ one has $e=1$, and $b/e^d=b/1$, while $e^db=0$ implies $b=(1-e)b$ (the case $d=0$ gives $b=0$). Thus $f^{\wedge}$ induces $Q_{\widehat A}/(1-e^{\wedge})\simeq P_{\widehat A}$.

source.place: Tag 00EE (lemma-disjoint-decomposition); schemes.tex Tags 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine), 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves); displayed elementary idempotent localization calculation

proof.text: Multiplication by $e^{\wedge}$ identifies $Q_{\widehat A}/(1-e^{\wedge})$ with the corner $e^{\wedge}Q_{\widehat A}$, whose identity is $e^{\wedge}$: the inverse sends $e^{\wedge}q$ to the class of $q$. Composing the inverse of the preceding isomorphism with this corner inclusion gives an additive multiplicative $\widehat A$-linear map $g^{\wedge}:P_{\widehat A}\to Q_{\widehat A}$ with $g^{\wedge}(1)=e^{\wedge}$, $f^{\wedge}g^{\wedge}=1$, and $g^{\wedge}f^{\wedge}(q)=e^{\wedge}q$. Here $g^{\wedge}$ is allowed to be nonunital. Choose polynomial representatives $F_j(x)$ of $f^{\wedge}(y_j)$, $G_i(y)$ of $g^{\wedge}(x_i)$, and $E(y)$ of $e^{\wedge}$, all with coefficients in $\widehat A$. Fix their finite monomial supports; their coefficients will be unknowns.

source.place: Elementary quotient and idempotent-corner calculation; Tag 00F3 finite presentations

proof.text: For coefficients in any $A$-algebra $R$, use the same supports for $F_j,G_i,E$. Impose $s_l(F)\in(r)$, $E^2-E\in(s)$, and $EG_i-G_i\in(s)$. For $p(x)=\sum_\alpha c_\alpha x^\alpha$, write $T(p)=c_0E+\sum_{\alpha\ne0}c_\alpha G^\alpha$ and impose $T(r_l)\in(s)$ for every relation of $P$. Then $f:Q_R\to P_R$, $y_j\mapsto F_j$, is a unital algebra map. Modulo $(s)$ the relations $E^2=E$ and $EG_i=G_i$ make $T$ additive, $R$-linear and multiplicative, with $T(1)=E$: multiply two monomials, treating a constant as a multiple of $E$. Since $T(r_lh)=T(r_l)T(h)$, it annihilates $(r)$ and induces $g:P_R\to Q_R$ with $g(1)=E$.

source.place: Elementary polynomial evaluation and quotient factorization; Tag 00F3

proof.text: Also impose $E(F)-1\in(r)$, $G_i(F)-x_i\in(r)$ and $T(F_j)-Ey_j\in(s)$. The first two sets say $fg=1_{P_R}$, since both sides are unital $R$-algebra maps agreeing on $x_i$. The third set says $gf(q)=Eq$ for all $q\in Q_R$: both maps are additive multiplicative $R$-linear maps with value $E$ at $1$, and they agree on $y_j$, hence on all polynomial expressions. These are finite lists even if some presentation has no generators or no relations. The chosen completion coefficients satisfy every imposed condition by their construction.

source.place: Elementary verification on generators, retaining the idempotent as the identity of the corner

proof.text:
Represent the fixed multiplication, identity and inverse maps of $X$ by polynomials $D_i^P(x,x')$, elements $c_i^P\in A$, and polynomials $I_i^P(x)$, respectively. Represent those of $Y$ by $D_j^Q(y,y')$, $c_j^Q$, $I_j^Q(y)$. This is possible by the presentations in Step 1 and the affine-spectrum correspondence. Impose, for each $j$, the three further identities
$$F_j(D^P(x,x'))-D_j^Q(F(x),F(x'))\in(r(x),r(x')),$$
$$F_j(c^P)-c_j^Q=0,\qquad F_j(I^P(x))-I_j^Q(F(x))\in(r).$$
They say exactly $\Delta_Pf=(f\otimes f)\Delta_Q$, $\epsilon_Pf=\epsilon_Q$, and $S_Pf=fS_Q$, checked on the generators $y_j$. Dualizing by the affine-spectrum correspondence gives compatibility with multiplication, identity and inverse. The given $v$ satisfies these equations. Neither cocommutativity of $\Delta$ nor any flatness is needed.

source.place: Tags 01I4, 01JQ, affine products; elementary dualization of the three group diagrams specified in the item

proof.text: Each requirement above, other than a scalar equality, has the form $H\in(t_1,\ldots,t_d)$ in a polynomial ring over $R$, where the fixed list $t$ is $(r(x))$, $(s(y))$ or $(r(x),r(x'))$. At the given completion solution choose actual polynomial witnesses $B_1,\ldots,B_d$ with $H=\sum_l B_lt_l$. This is exactly membership in the ideal generated by $t$. Choose such witnesses for every requirement, a finite list, and fix each witness's finite monomial support. For the empty list of relations, membership means the polynomial $H$ itself is zero and no witnesses are required. Introduce one more unknown for each witness coefficient.

source.place: Elementary finite ideal-membership witnesses in polynomial quotients, as in the generators-and-relations arguments of Tags 00QO and 05N8

proof.text: Replace every membership requirement by the polynomial identity $H-\sum_lB_lt_l=0$, and compare coefficients of all monomials occurring in that expression. Each coefficient is a polynomial over $A$ in the finitely many unknown coefficients of $F,G,E$ and the witnesses: substitution, multiplication and addition of finite polynomials use finitely many sums and products. Include the scalar equations from Step 6. Thus there is one finite system $h_1(z)=\cdots=h_c(z)=0$ over $A$ with a specified solution $\widehat z$ in $\widehat A$. Every solution over any $A$-algebra supplies all identities of Steps 4--6. This uses equality of polynomials, not coefficientwise equality of classes in a quotient. The supports bound the selected solution and witnesses, and need not parametrize every possible map.

source.place: Elementary coefficient comparison using the definition of a multivariable polynomial as a finite coefficient family

proof.text: Apply henselian-pair approximation with $I=\mathfrak m$, $N=1$ to the finite system of Step 8. The henselian local hypothesis says that $(A,\mathfrak m)$ is henselian; the G-ring hypothesis includes that $A$ is Noetherian. The completion is precisely the completion in the cited approximation theorem. It therefore supplies $z\in A^d$ satisfying every $h_l(z)=0$ with $\widehat z_l-\iota(z_l)\in\mathfrak m\widehat A$ for every coordinate. In particular this approximates the coefficients of $F$ together with the idempotent, inverse and relation-membership witnesses, so all their identities remain exact over $A$.

Decode the solution $z$ by Steps 4--5, now with $R=A$. We obtain an algebra map $f:Q\to P$, an idempotent $e\in Q$, and an additive multiplicative $A$-linear map $g:P\to Q$ with $g(1)=e$, $fg=1$ and $gf(q)=eq$. Thus $f$ is surjective. Also $f(e)=1$, so $(1-e)Q\subseteq\ker f$; if $f(q)=0$ then $eq=gf(q)=0$ and $q=(1-e)q$, proving $\ker f=(1-e)Q$. Consequently $f$ induces an isomorphism $Q/(1-e)\simeq P$. This deduction does not require $g$ to be a unital map to $Q$.

source.place: Elementary inverse and kernel computation from the explicit identities

proof.text: Let $w=\operatorname{Spec}f:X\to Y$. The three sets of equations of Step 6, which hold over $A$, say that $w$ preserves all the specified group operations: equality on the algebra generators implies equality of the corresponding scheme maps. For multiplication the common source has algebra $P\otimes_AP$, as supplied by the affine-fibre-product theorem; for identity it is $A$; for inverse it is $P$. Hence $w$ is an $A$-group homomorphism.

source.place: Tags 01I4, 01JQ; affine-spectrum faithfulness applied separately to the three group diagrams

proof.text: The kernel description identifies $w$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(Q/(1-e))\to\operatorname{Spec}Q$, which is a closed immersion by the affine characterization. The elementary idempotent calculation of Step 2 identifies its quotient algebra, compatibly with the map from $Q$, with $Q_e$. The affine-basic-open theorem identifies $\operatorname{Spec}Q_e$ with the open subscheme $D(e)$, and the clopen-idempotent theorem says $D(e)$ is also closed. Thus $w$ is an open immersion as well as a closed immersion.

source.place: Tags 01QO (affine closed immersions), 01I3 and 01HV (basic-open affine structure); algebra.tex Tag 00EE

proof.text: Since $A$ is Noetherian, its maximal ideal is finitely generated. Completion modulo this ideal is canonically $A/\mathfrak m=k$ by the completion-mod-power theorem with $N=1$. Every coefficient of $F_j$ from $z$ therefore has the same image in $k$ as the corresponding coefficient in the chosen representative of $f^{\wedge}(y_j)$. Evaluation gives identical images of every $y_j$ in $P\otimes_Ak$, so the two $k$-algebra maps $Q\otimes_Ak\to P\otimes_Ak$ are equal. The affine-spectrum correspondence gives $w_k=v_k$. Only this residue equality follows from approximation; none of the argument requires equality of the maps over $\widehat A$.

proof_origin.place: Finite polynomial certificate argument written by Q28, using Tag 0AH5 and the cited affine/idempotent results; the encoding is explicit in Steps 3--8.
